description: A heading is turned through `const titleAngle = normalizeAngle(ta);` in `assembleTitleGroup`, and a caption is not — `assembleLabelTitle` hands `labelAngle` to the same two rules exactly as it was written. The asymmetry is upstream's and it is visible, because both rules are written as a chain of comparisons against a number between zero and three hundred and sixty: a heading turned to minus one hundred degrees is a heading turned to two hundred and sixty, and two hundred and sixty is caught by `225 < angle && angle < 315` and by the arm that reads `45 <= angle && angle <= 135`, where minus one hundred falls through the first and is caught instead by `angle <= 45`. So this chart's column heading is baselined `middle` and its row heading `bottom`; handing the number over as it was written would baseline them `bottom` and `middle`, which is the same pair of words on the wrong pair of headings. The anchors show the other half of `defaultHeaderGuideAlign`. The column heading is anchored at the start, which aligns it `left` whatever the turn, and puts it against band 0 of the column band — `LAYOUT_TITLE_BAND.column.start`. The row heading must not change: it anchors itself `middle`, which is the default the function declares in its own signature — `anchor: TitleAnchor = 'middle'` — and so falls past both `case` arms to the angle, taking `left` from the turn instead of from the anchor; and `middle` has no entry in either row of `LAYOUT_TITLE_BAND`, so `getLayoutTitleBand` answers nothing and the layout is left with a `titleBand` naming the column alone rather than both bands.
